title: Haya Banana Wine
localName: Omuramba — Divai ya Ndizi ya Wahaya
community: Haya people of Kagera — the banana wine of the Great Lakes
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Haya Omuramba — the banana wine of the Kagera region. Ripe bananas fermented with sorghum for 5—7 days into a clear, lightly alcoholic beverage of remarkable quality. One of East Africa's finest traditional fermented drinks — made by the Haya people of Tanzania's Great Lakes region.
longDesc: Omuramba banana wine is the Haya's most important ceremonial drink — made for weddings, funerals, birth celebrations, and royal occasions. It is distinct from Chaga mbege (TZA242) in its longer fermentation, use of different banana varieties, and the addition of sorghum. The result is a clearer, more refined fermented beverage.
ingredients: 10 kg very ripe cooking bananas — not dessert bananas
1 kg sorghum grain — roasted and ground
equipment: Large clay or food-grade fermentation vessel
Gourds or clean containers for serving
steps: Peel bananas. Knead vigorously until completely mashed into a liquid pulp.
Add roasted sorghum flour. Mix well.
Transfer to a clean fermentation vessel.
Cover with banana leaves and a cloth.
After 5—7 days, strain through cloth, pressing firmly.
The strained liquid is omuramba — serve at room temperature.
chefTips: The kneading of the bananas is the most labour-intensive step — it must be thorough.
Temperature and time determine sweetness vs sourness.
The sorghum provides yeast and structure.
cookingScience: See TZA242 for banana fermentation science. Omuramba ferments longer and is strained more thoroughly than mbege — producing a clearer, more wine-like beverage with higher alcohol content and less residual sweetness.
sustainabilityTips: Using over-ripe bananas — the harvest surplus that would otherwise go to waste.
culturalNote: Omuramba is the wine of the Haya kingdom — the drink that was served at the courts of the Haya kings and that still defines every important Haya ceremony. The Haya are Tanzania's great banana wine makers, and omuramba is their masterpiece.
